$comment: Per-repo settings for the usiatech-engineering plugin. Copy to .claude/engineering.json and adjust.

git.$comment: Optional semver bump on every release: set versionFiles (the files that hold the version, e.g. ["package.json"]), optionally changelogFile (gets a new row per release), and tagFormat "vX.Y.Z". The repo needs a first vX.Y.Z tag made by hand. Leave versionFiles out to keep date tags and no bump. See the README under Semver bump.

reviewerModels.$comment: Optional model per reviewer agent, keyed by agent name: "sonnet", "opus", "haiku" or "inherit" (the session's model). Read from the base branch. A reviewer with no entry runs on its agent file's model: sonnet for convention, silent-failure, supply-chain and workflow reviewers, opus for governance and security. E.g. {"security-reviewer": "sonnet"}.

session.$comment: Advice from scripts/session-check.mjs at the start of release and approve-plan. contextAdvisoryTokens (default 300000, a positive whole number) is the context size above which it recommends compacting or a fresh session, once per session. Read from the base branch.

tickets.$comment: Ticket tracker for clarify, to-spec, to-tickets, approve-plan, verify and release: "github" (the default) or "jira". With no tickets section the Jira steps don't run. For Jira set tracker to "jira" and add "jira": {"site": "https://example.atlassian.net", "project": "ESP", "issueType": "Subtask", "parent": "ESP-27" (optional), "statuses": {"started": "In Progress", "devComplete": "...", "testingStarted": "...", "testingComplete": "In Testing", "merged": "Ready for Release", "released": "Released"} (each optional; "verified" is another name for testingComplete), "cloudId" and "transitions": {"started": "21", ...} (optional transition IDs), "transport": "connector" (the default: every Jira write goes through the Atlassian connector) or "api" (the script only, with credentials from the JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN environment variables; the token is sent only to an .atlassian.net site or the JIRA_SITE host)}. Repos that rely on the Jira API must set "transport": "api". Moves never go backwards. Jira failures are never retried and never undo git steps. See the README under Jira tracker and ADR 0003.

governance.$comment: Guard settings. Commands are case-insensitive regexes. Defaults already cover destructive git/SQL/rm, curl|sh, --no-verify, dependency adds, remote/infra commands, secrets reads and sudo. allowlist suppresses one workflow/dependency finding by rule ID plus a path glob or package name (still reported, never blocks); a wf-* entry needs one literal file path and can't cover wf-unparsed, otherwise it suppresses nothing and is reported as wf-allowlist-ignored, e.g. {"rule": "wf-unpinned-action", "path": ".github/workflows/pr-governance.yml", "reason": "..."} or {"rule": "sc-install-script", "package": "esbuild", "reason": "postinstall only fetches its platform binary"}; it ships empty. trustedWritePaths (writes outside the project that don't ask, still logged as trusted; the values shown are the defaults, [] asks again) and planEdits ("allow" lets plan edits that only change evidence, task ticks or the change log through; "ask" asks for every plan edit; "all" trusts every plan and archive write, still logged, so the governance-reviewer becomes the only scope check on plan changes) are explained in the README under Trusted writes. approvalLabel and requirementRefPattern (null = default C-number/FR/AC/ADR/D-item/§/#issue) are also used by the PR governance workflow. ESP-166 (ADR-0005): each restriction from agentsFiles to uncheckable, and each governance.commands key, takes "deny", "ask" or "allow"; the values shown are the defaults, and "allow" is logged as allowed-by-config. agentsFiles to dependencyFiles set the askPaths groups (the PR workflow reads them too). Edits to .claude/engineering.json, .claude/settings*.json, .claude/hooks/**, .claude/agents/** and any .git folder or file always ask. adrEdits decides edits under adrPaths instead of the plan's Files list. uncheckable covers edits the guard can't read (8.3 short names, links, a failed lookup). bypass: true turns every other ask into an allow, logged as bypassed; denies and destructive commands stay. See the README under Guard settings.

commands.$comment: Non-destructive command rules, each "deny", "ask" or "allow". Destructive commands have no key and always keep their deny or ask: the built-in denies, force push, discarding work, branch deletes, history rewrites, recursive delete, destructive SQL and database resets.
